records.content_title: Flu, RSV or COVID-19? How Parents Can Tell Which Respiratory Illness Their Child Has
records.content: A stuffy nose, cough and fever can leave any parent guessing. Is it a cold, flu, COVID-19 or respiratory syncytial virus, better known as RSV? The four illnesses overlap so much that symptoms alone rarely settle the question, per the American Academy of Pediatrics . A few clues can still help families know what to watch out for. What Each Illness Looks Like RSV often starts like a cold but can affect breathing. Along with fever, cough and congestion, children may wheeze, breathe fast, flare their nostrils or grunt. Some babies eat poorly. Symptoms tend to be worst around the third to fifth day and can last one to two weeks. The flu usually hits harder. Chills, headache, body aches and a dry cough are common and some children vomit or have diarrhea. Symptoms typically appear one to four days after exposure. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommended a yearly flu shot for everyone 6 months and older. BY: UNSPLASH COVID-19 could look much like the flu, with fatigue, muscle aches, sore throat and congestion. Some children lose taste or smell. Symptoms show up two to 14 days after infection, a longer window than the flu's. The common cold is generally milder, with sneezing, a sore throat and slightly swollen glands. Healthy children catch six to 10 colds a year. A child can catch more than one virus at a time, such as the flu and COVID-19. A second problem, including bronchiolitis, pneumonia or an ear or sinus infection, can also follow. A pediatrician may order a test if a diagnosis matters for treatment. When to Call the Doctor Flu, RSV, COVID-19 and the common cold share many of the same symptoms. BY: UNSPLASH Contact a pediatrician if a child is breathing rapidly, flaring their nostrils, wheezing, grunting or struggling for breath or if the chest pulls in with each breath. Other warning signs include vomiting for more than 24 hours, bloody diarrhea, unusual drowsiness, poor feeding and dehydration. Fever matters, too. Please call if any child has a temperature above 104 degrees Fahrenheit or above 103 degrees for more than 24 hours. For babies younger than 2 months, a fever above 100.4 degrees also warrants a call. How to Prevent Respiratory Illnesses Fast breathing, wheezing or a chest that pulls in with each breath are warning signs. BY: UNSPLASH The academy recommended a yearly flu vaccine for everyone 6 months and older, a message it renewed for 2026-27 after a severe season in which 190 children died. About 85 percent of pediatric flu deaths occur in unvaccinated children and only 49.4% of children ages 6 months to 17 years had been vaccinated as of May, the report said . The academy also recommended this season's COVID-19 vaccine for all children 6 through 23 months and for older children up to 18 at higher risk. For RSV, it recommended immunization for infants younger than 8 months entering their first season, unless the mother was vaccinated during pregnancy and for some high-risk children 8 through 19 months

records.content: 24/7 LiveRaleighDurhamFayettevilleSurrounding Area 41° HEALTH & FITNESS Parents urged to watch for RSV symptoms as Thanksgiving approaches Doctors are urging families to take precautions against RSV and other respiratory illnesses as Thanksgiving gatherings approach. ByPenelope Lopez Wednesday, November 18, 2026 1:09PM Share Follow ABC11 on Google FAYETTEVILLE, NC (WTVD) -- Respiratory illnesses accounted for 9% of emergency department visits in North Carolina, up from 8.5% the previous week, according to the state Department of Health and Human Services. With Thanksgiving approaching, doctors are urging families to take precautions to help limit the spread of respiratory viruses, particularly around babies and young children. Dr. Ashlee Roybal, who works in the pediatric intensive care unit at Cape Fear Valley Medical Center, said she saw her first case of respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV, of the year this week. She said basic prevention measures, including frequent handwashing, can help reduce transmission. "Primarily washing hands. While it sounds simple, people don't always appreciate how easily germs spread. Touching things without washing your hands frequently throughout the day is a great way to pick up and transmit viruses," Roybal said. People who are sick should try to avoid close contact with others, especially infants. Masks can also help reduce the spread of respiratory viruses, Roybal said. "If you're sick, try to isolate yourself. Using face masks is a great way to prevent the spread because many of these viruses are transmitted through respiratory droplets. Something as simple as coughing or sneezing can spread those droplets," Roybal said. In infants, RSV can initially resemble a common cold. Symptoms can include congestion, fever and difficulty breathing, Roybal said. Some babies may also become dehydrated or have trouble feeding. "What we primarily see in younger infants is a stuffy nose, congestion and fever. Those symptoms can lead to difficulty breathing. We can also see dehydration and difficulty feeding," Roybal said. RSV and the flu can cause similar symptoms. Roybal advised parents to watch for signs that a child is struggling to breathe, including head bobbing, belly breathing and nasal flaring. Roybal said parents may use fever-reducing medicine to help children feel more comfortable while following age guidelines. Top Stories Authorities in Turkey search for lion seen prowling near Istanbul More rain to affect Thanksgiving travel Drought reveals remnants of communities beneath Jordan Lake in North Carolina "Tylenol and Motrin can be helpful for children older than 6 months. For infants younger than 6 months, I recommend using Tylenol only. The goal is to make them more comfortable and reduce fevers," Roybal said. Parents should seek medical attention if a child is breathing very rapidly, becomes unusually irritable, has difficulty eating or drinking, or coughs so much that it leads to vomiting, Roybal said. "If they're breathing so fast that they're fussy and irritable, not able to eat or drink well, or coughing so much that they're vomiting, those are concerning signs," Roybal said. Health officials are urging people to take precautions as respiratory illnesses increase, including through the holiday season. records.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, November 25, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Respiratory Insults Trigger a Conserved Hardwired Differentiation Program in Lung Macrophages by November 24, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Respiratory Insults Trigger a Conserved Hardwired Differentiation Program in Lung Macrophages Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram When the respiratory tract encounters severe infectious pathogens or sterile injuries, tissue-resident alveolar macrophages derived from embryonic precursors frequently undergo substantial depletion and are subsequently replaced by circulating monocytes. For years, immunologists hypothesized that incoming blood monocytes were plastic entities whose ultimate phenotype and functional identity were dictated by the specific inflammatory environment present in the damaged lung. In a comprehensive study published in Nature Immunology, a research team led by Chrysante S. Iliakis, Wouter T’Jonck, Isobel C. Mouat, Andreas Wack, and Calum C. Bain has challenged this paradigm. Utilizing rigorous genetic fate-mapping models, single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, metabolic assays, and high-dimensional spectral flow cytometry in C57BL/6 mice, the investigators evaluated the cellular dynamics of alveolar macrophage replacement across three distinct lung challenges: respiratory syncytial virus infection, influenza A virus infection, and sterile macrophage depletion mediated by intratracheal clodronate liposomes. Their findings reveal that monocyte-derived alveolar macrophages follow a strictly conserved, stereotypic developmental blueprint irrespective of the nature or inflammatory intensity of the initial lung insult, acquiring prolonged proliferative, metabolic, and immunoreactive traits governed by a cell-intrinsic transcription factor checkpoint. To establish the foundational kinetics of macrophage replacement in infectious settings, the authors first inoculated adult mice intranasally with the human A2 strain of respiratory syncytial virus. Viral replication, measured by viral L-gene mRNA expression in lung tissue, peaked sharply at two days post-infection and became completely undetectable by fourteen days, coinciding with a robust type I interferon surge and an accumulation of cellular debris in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Mice inoculated with ultraviolet-inactivated virus showed no such viral replication or interferon responses. Flow cytometric analysis of the bronchoalveolar space revealed an immediate collapse of the resident alveolar macrophage pool within twelve to forty-eight hours, accompanied by a steep reduction in Ki67-positive proliferating macrophages and a significant increase in Annexin V-positive apoptotic cells. The overall macrophage population returned to baseline numbers by seven days post-infection, during which an early influx of Ly6G-positive neutrophils peaked at twenty-four hours, followed by a substantial wave of recruited Ly6C-high monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages that peaked at seven days before maturing into cells expressing major histocompatibility complex class II and MerTK. To track the ultimate fate and longevity of these recruited cells without ambiguity, the investigators used Ms4a3Cre; Rosa26-CAG-LSL-tdTomato reporter mice, in which bone marrow-derived granulocyte-monocyte progenitors and their progeny are indelibly marked by red fluorescent tdTomato expression, leaving embryonically derived alveolar macrophages unlabeled. Following respiratory syncytial virus infection, tdTomato-positive myeloid cells occupied the neutrophil and monocyte compartments during the first week. Notably, newly formed monocyte-derived alveolar macrophages retained lower surface levels of SiglecF than resident fetal-derived macrophages for over two months. By four and a half months post-infection, tdTomato chimerism within the alveolar macrophage niche reached parity with circulating blood monocytes, a phenomenon absent in uninfected or ultraviolet-inactivated control mice. Parallel experiments employing tissue-protected bone marrow chimeric mice, in which host lungs were shielded with lead during irradiation prior to reconstitution, corroborated this progressive, long-term domination of the alveolar compartment by bone marrow-derived cells. Discover more Engineering Job Board Research Paper Access Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges The progressive accumulation of monocyte-derived alveolar macrophages could theoretically stem from continuous de novo recruitment from the blood or from the expansion of cells recruited during the acute phase of infection. To resolve this question, the researchers utilized an inducible Ccr2Cre-ERT2; Rosa26-CAG-LSL-tdTomato temporal labeling model. A single oral dose of tamoxifen administered twenty-four hours before respiratory syncytial virus challenge selectively labeled circulating classical monocytes, which decayed rapidly from the bloodstream due to physiological turnover while leaving resident alveolar macrophages unlabeled. Assessing bronchoalveolar lavage fluid two months later revealed that approximately half of all alveolar macrophages were tdTomato-positive, proving that cells recruited during acute infection persist long term. Conversely, when tamoxifen was delivered thirty-five days after viral infection, subsequent analysis at fifty-six days showed no labeling in the alveolar macrophage pool, demonstrating that monocyte recruitment is restricted to a narrow acute window. Three-dimensional confocal microscopy and nearest-neighbor spatial distribution analyses of cleared lung sections further established that these newly integrated monocyte-derived macrophages did not segregate into isolated architectural niches, but rather interspersed directly alongside fetal-derived macrophages within the same alveoli. Dissecting the stepwise maturation of these cells, the researchers isolated sequential populations defined by surface markers along a differentiation continuum from CD11b-positive to SiglecF-low and finally SiglecF-high macrophages. Bulk RNA sequencing revealed a gradual downregulation of classical monocyte transcripts, such as Ccr2 and Cd93, alongside the coordinated induction of mature alveolar macrophage genes, including Pparg, Marco, Fabp1, and Epcam, accompanied by enhanced STAT5 phosphorylation upon granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor stimulation. Flow cytometric metabolic profiling demonstrated that transitioning CD11b-positive cells possessed an energetic phenotype strikingly distinct from mature macrophages, exhibiting reduced mitochondrial mass and reduced uptake of the long-chain fatty acid BODIPY-C16. Single-cell metabolic profiling via translation translation-inhibition assays further confirmed that developing monocyte-derived macrophages underwent a progressive increase in mitochondrial dependence for adenosine triphosphate production as they differentiated, accompanied by a relative decline in glucose reliance. Transcriptomic pairwise comparisons along the developmental continuum pinpointed the transition from the CD11b-positive intermediate to the SiglecF-low state as the site of the largest molecular shift, characterized by hundreds of differentially expressed genes heavily enriched in cell cycle and proliferation pathways. Flow cytometry and short-term 5-ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine pulse-chase labeling confirmed that while CD11b-positive precursors were largely quiescent, SiglecF-low monocyte-derived macrophages exhibited a dramatic acquisition of suprahomeostatic proliferative capacity that persisted for months. Investigating candidate transcriptional regulators revealed that the transcription factor early growth response 2, or EGR2, was sharply upregulated early during this transition. To test its functional necessity, the authors generated myeloid-specific Lyz2Cre; Egr2fl/fl knockout mice. Following viral challenge, EGR2-deficient monocytes were recruited normally to the lungs at two weeks but subsequently failed to progress beyond the CD11b-positive stage. Instead of expanding into SiglecF-low proliferating cells, EGR2-deficient CD11b-positive macrophages persisted abnormally at one month, displayed elevated Annexin V staining, and underwent extensive cell death without acquiring self-renewal capacity. To definitively prove that EGR2 operates via cell-intrinsic mechanisms rather than through an altered microenvironment, the authors established competitive mixed bone marrow chimeras by transferring a one-to-one mixture of wild-type CD45.1-positive and Lyz2Cre; Egr2fl/fl CD45.2-positive donor bone marrow into busulfan-conditioned, immunodeficient Ccr2-null Rag2-null recipient mice. Following respiratory syncytial virus challenge, both donor genotypes contributed equally to the initial monocyte infiltrate at fourteen days post-infection. However, by one month, the alveolar macrophage compartment was overwhelmingly dominated by wild-type cells. Wild-type monocyte-derived cells successfully shed CD11b, upregulated SiglecF, CD2, EpCAM, and CD169, and entered active cell cycle, whereas EGR2-deficient counterparts remained arrested in the CD11b-positive state and suffered elevated apoptosis. Complementary adoptive transfer experiments, in which sorted CD11b-positive macrophages from infected donors were transferred intratracheally into clodronate-conditioned reporter recipients, similarly showed that wild-type cells engrafted, down-regulated CD11b, and proliferated vigorously, while EGR2-deficient donor cells completely failed to integrate or incorporate 5-ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine, solidifying EGR2 as an indispensable molecular checkpoint for macrophage maturation. To determine the long-term transcriptional trajectory of integrated monocyte-derived macrophages versus original resident cells, the authors performed bulk RNA sequencing on sorted congenic subsets from busulfan chimeric mice up to four months after viral clearance. At one month post-infection, monocyte-derived macrophages exhibited high expression of interferon response genes and monocyte-associated inflammatory chemokines, including Ccl2, Ccl7, Cd40, and Spp1. By contrast, co-existing fetal-derived macrophages down-regulated baseline interferon-stimulated genes and showed diminished expression of typical identity genes. Although monocyte-derived macrophages gradually aligned transcriptionally with resident cells over four months, notable differences persisted, including sustained elevation of major histocompatibility complex class II machinery such as H2-Aa, H2-Ab1, and Ciita in monocyte descendants, while fetal-derived cells preferentially maintained higher expression of metabolic regulators such as Slc7a11 and Nlrx1. The researchers next asked whether this developmental trajectory was unique to viral infection or represented a universal program across diverse lung injuries. They employed intratracheal clodronate liposomes, which eliminated ninety percent of alveolar macrophages in the absence of infectious pathogens, overt vascular permeability, lung tissue albumin leakage, or systemic weight loss. High-dimensional flow cytometry coupled with Phenograph unsupervised clustering revealed that monocyte-derived cells elicited by sterile clodronate administration transitioned through the exact same Ly6C-positive, CD11b-positive, and SiglecF-positive progression observed after respiratory syncytial virus and influenza A virus infections. Clodronate-elicited monocytes navigated this shared trajectory with significantly accelerated kinetics, reaching the SiglecF-low and mature states weeks faster than virus-elicited cells. Despite these kinetic differences, direct comparative analysis revealed that monocyte-derived macrophages from all three contexts shared nearly identical transcriptional profiles, displayed identical impairments in long-chain fatty acid uptake and peroxisome mass, maintained identical reductions in mitochondrial reliance, and sustained equivalent elevated proliferative rates in vivo. Finally, the authors evaluated whether this conserved ontogenetic trajectory translates into uniform immunological protection. When stimulated ex vivo with the toll-like receptor 2 agonist Pam3CSK4, monocyte-derived macrophages from all recruitment models exhibited identical, hyper-responsive cytokine secretion profiles, releasing massive amounts of interleukin-6, interleukin-1, and inflammatory chemokines, whereas co-existing fetal-derived macrophages remained consistently hyporesponsive. Total alveolar macrophages from all challenge models showed heightened responsiveness to bacterial lipopolysaccharide and CpG oligonucleotides. To determine whether this monocyte legacy conferred physiological defense, mice previously conditioned with sterile clodronate liposomes or influenza A virus were subsequently challenged with a lethal dose of Streptococcus pneumoniae strain TIGR4. Remarkably, mice possessing monocyte-derived alveolar macrophages from either sterile depletion or prior viral infection exhibited marked resistance to secondary bacterial pneumonia, displaying significantly enhanced cumulative survival, reduced body weight loss, and lower clinical morbidity scores compared to control mice. The investigators concluded that the distinct immunological properties of monocyte-derived alveolar macrophages are hardwired by their monocyte ontogeny rather than imprinted by viral pathology, providing robust antibacterial protection while underscoring that therapeutic targeting of alveolar macrophage reprogramming must account for cellular lineage. Autumn and winter respiratory illnesses represent a major public health priority and cause considerable morbidity. To track disease dynamics, Germany relies on both pathogen-specific and syndromic surveillance indicators, which monitor general practitioner visits alongside inpatient hospitalizations. The surveillance initiative focused primarily on general practitioner consultations for acute respiratory infections and hospital admissions for severe acute respiratory infections. A total of eight separate models generated nowcasts and forward predictions for these syndromic measures. Additionally, the system monitored laboratory-confirmed infections of seasonal influenza and respiratory syncytial virus, utilizing a single designated forecasting model for each specific pathogen. Because surveillance indicators in Germany are routinely subject to retrospective data revisions, modeling groups coupled all forward projections with an initial nowcasting step to correct for reporting delays. For acute respiratory infections and severe acute respiratory infections, researchers combined the individual model outputs into an ensemble forecast. Quantitative assessments showed that nowcasts delivered convincing performance across the season, though reporting changes during the Christmas break caused an upward bias in early January. Overall, the forward forecasts proved well-calibrated, with most models outperforming simple persistence baselines. When evaluating age-stratified targets, the performance advantages of the predictive models over simple baseline comparisons were statistically significant. However, anticipating the exact timing and magnitude of disease peaks proved challenging across the modeling consortium. Many participating models projected curves that were too flat and predicted turnaround dates that occurred too early, such as projecting late January peaks rather than the mid-February peak observed for severe acute respiratory infections. Although the combined ensemble forecast ranked among the best-performing tools throughout the season, it did not consistently outperform the strongest individual models, marking a notable difference from earlier collaborative forecasting efforts during the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on these quantitative evaluations, the study authors outlined organizational insights and structural lessons to guide future collaborative disease forecasting projects in post-pandemic public health systems. records.content: 基于噬菌体免疫沉淀测序的出生至幼儿期泛病毒血清学纵向研究揭示病毒血清转化的早期预测因素 《Cell Reports Medicine》:Longitudinal pan-viral serology from birth to early childhood reveals early-life predictors of viral seroconversion 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月25日 来源:Cell Reports Medicine 14.0 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Article 幼儿期的特征是免疫系统尚在发育且病毒感染普遍流行,这可能影响儿童的长期健康。研究人员利用噬菌体免疫沉淀测序(PhIP-seq)技术,检测了963对脐带血与幼儿期血浆样本中对覆盖所有已知人类病毒蛋白质组的肽段的抗体反应性。在生命最初几年中,儿童发生对肠道病毒、腺病毒和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)的血清转化。研究人员鉴定了具有RSV A/B型特异性抗体反应的儿童,并描述了RSV A/B型特异性抗体的靶标。研究人员还系统评估了生命早期因素与病毒血清转化之间的关联,发现巨细胞病毒(CMV)血清阳性母亲的母乳喂养是儿童CMV血清转化的最强预测因素。该研究建立了在出生队列中系统探索抗病毒抗体反应组的蓝图,鉴定了预测病毒血清转化的可改变因素,并产生了将为发育免疫系统持续研究提供信息的见解。 **研究背景** 观看单细胞测序入门大讲堂录播视频&资料下载 领 取 病毒感染给人类健康带来沉重负担,从普通感冒、肠炎等轻症到艾滋病、肝炎和危及生命的肺炎等重症。以呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)为例,2009至2019年间,RSV占美国婴儿住院的近10%。除急性感染的影响外,病毒感染还可诱导保护性抗病毒免疫应答和/或导致与免疫功能障碍相关的病理后遗症。因此,病毒感染是儿童期及以后个体健康的关键决定因素。噬菌体免疫沉淀测序(PhIP-seq)结合寡核苷酸编码肽库可用于高通量分析血清抗体反应性。VirScan文库包含覆盖所有已知感染人类病毒的肽段,对多种病毒感染已显示出超过90%的敏感性和特异性。将VirScan应用于出生队列可为了解生命早期病毒暴露及由此产生的免疫应答提供见解。波士顿出生队列(BBC)在出生时招募母婴对,以评估早产的原因和后果,部分儿童接受了纵向随访。病毒感染和抗病毒免疫是可能与各种健康结局相关的主要未探索因素。为评估对全人类病毒组的血清学暴露和/或疫苗接种证据,研究人员使用VirScan对BBC中963对脐带血和幼儿期血浆样本的病毒抗体反应性进行了编目。 **关键技术方法** 研究人员采用噬菌体免疫沉淀测序(PhIP-seq)技术,利用VirScan肽库(覆盖所有已知人类病毒蛋白质组)对来自波士顿出生队列(BBC)的963对脐带血和幼儿期血浆样本(采集于2000年9月至2012年9月,儿童采血年龄0.47至4.96岁)进行抗体反应性分析。通过下一代测序(Illumina NovaSeq6000)检测抗体结合噬菌体编码DNA。采用病毒聚合反应性评分(VARscore)量化抗体反应,并通过传统CMV IgG酶联免疫吸附试验(ELISA)对178份样本进行验证。研究人员建立线性模型去除母源性抗体反应性,并采用多因素逻辑回归分析行为与人口学因素与血清转化的关联。 **研究结果** **母体与儿童抗病毒抗体反应的系统比较** 胎儿循环接收经胎盘转移的母体抗体,可在出生后持续6至9个月。研究人员评估了脐带血与配对儿童血浆抗病毒抗体谱随出生后时间的相关性。儿童与母亲抗体谱的相关性最初较高,呈指数衰减,然后上升至平台期。初始衰减归因于母源性抗体的丢失,随后的上升归因于对流行病毒免疫优势表位应答的积累。2岁及以上儿童与配对脐带血的相关性强于与非配对脐带血的相关性。研究人员建立了统一的VARscore阈值1.937(特异性0.994,敏感性0.982)定义血清阳性。基于VARscore,PhIP-seq检测的母体抗体半衰期为55.6天(95%置信区间:34.6-76.7天)。脐带血与儿童血清中病毒血清阳性率频繁不同,脐带血中更常检测到的差异最大病毒包括EBV、HSV1、流感B、RSV B、RSV A、HSV2、CMV、腺病毒C和水痘-带状疱疹病毒(VZV),儿童血清中更常检测到的为副肠孤病毒1和2。儿童中对鼻病毒和肠道病毒血清阳性率最高。 **MMR疫苗接种的抗体反应** 大多数脐带血对MMR所含病毒VARscore阴性。1岁以下儿童对这些病毒缺乏抗体。MMR组分VARscores在初次接种后数年内下降。接种疫苗后VARscores升高(Wilcoxon检验:麻疹p < 2.2e?16,腮腺炎p = 1.1e?14,风疹p < 2.2e?16)。VARscore作为疫苗接种预测因素的ROC曲线AUC分别为麻疹0.973、腮腺炎0.713、风疹0.988。2至3岁儿童中超过90%对MMR一种或多种病毒VARscore阳性,3至4岁及4岁以上儿童降至81%以上。 **肠道病毒、副肠孤病毒、哺乳动物腺病毒、诺如病毒、星状病毒和轮状病毒的抗体反应** 几乎所有脐带血样本含有对肠道病毒的抗体反应(99.9%,962/963)。绝大多数儿童也为肠道病毒血清阳性(97.5%,939/963)。母亲对哺乳动物腺病毒显示近乎普遍的血清阳性(97.5%,939/963),儿童抗体反应呈明显双峰分布,50.5%儿童为哺乳动物腺病毒血清阳性。1至2岁儿童中,99.6%为肠道病毒阳性,50.4%为哺乳动物腺病毒阳性,55.5%为诺如病毒阳性,29.3%为星状病毒阳性。对副肠孤病毒和轮状病毒的抗体反应在较大儿童中较少检测到,可能表明可检测抗体减弱。 parvovirus B19血清阳性率较低(3.2%,31/963),副流感病毒抗体反应常见(42.1%,405/963)。 **肺病毒和流感病毒的抗体反应** 绝大多数母亲对RSV A(99.9%,962/963)和RSV B(97.7%,941/963)显示抗体反应性,约半数儿童对这些病毒血清阳性(RSV A:51.7%,498/963;RSV B:43.1%,415/963)。1岁以下儿童中59.4%对RSV A和/或RSV B VARscore阳性,4岁及以上儿童超过95%阳性。脐带血对RSV A和RSV B抗体反应性紧密相关,然而儿童主要显示型特异性RSV抗体反应。 **RSV A和RSV B型特异性及交叉反应性表位反应性** 与RSV型VARscore相关性最强的肽段来源于相应的RSV G蛋白。VirScan检测的F蛋白抗体反应性与整体RSV抗体反应弱相关,但非型特异性。G蛋白胞外部分的几乎全部区域以型特异性方式被靶向,VARscore与含半胱氨酸套索的中心保守域反应性之间相关性最强。 **疱疹病毒的抗体反应** 脐带血样本对HSV1、HSV2、HHV3(VZV)、CMV和EBV的抗体反应性率远高于儿童血浆。BBC中HSV1 VARscore阳性率从1至2岁儿童的约9%增至4岁以上儿童的约40%。EBV VARscore阳性率从1至2岁儿童的约15%增至4岁以上儿童的约58%。1岁以下儿童CMV [0.110-0.531])和CMV阴性母亲纯配方奶喂养儿童(OR:0.147 [0.035-0.421])的CMV血清转化率降低。未接触多儿童托育的儿童与接触者相比OR为0.620 [0.441-0.868]。 **行为与人口学因素对病毒血清转化的影响** A/B型特异性血清阳性的儿童及无任何RSV抗体反应的儿童。具有RSV A或RSV records.content: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 08: Nurse Susana Azapyan administers a dose of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine to resident Abraham Hamamdjian at the Ararat Nursing Facility in the Mission Hills neighborhood of Los Angeles on January 8, 2021 in Los Angeles, California. Residents and staff at long term care facilities are on the CDC's highest priority list for vaccinations. While COVID-19 cases in nursing facilities represent just 5 percent of the total cases in California, they account for 35 percent of all Covid deaths in the state. Mario Tama/Getty Images The UK Health Security Agency's (UKHSA) new guide for adults over 65 in England is dated Thursday, November 19, and is on GOV.UK, but a healthy 66-year-old is offered flu, shingles and pneumococcal vaccines and not this autumn's COVID-19 or RSV shots. The autumn COVID-19 program and the RSV program for older adults both start at 75 for most people, so the leaflet's "over 65" label covers five vaccines with different starting ages. A reader checking their own coverage, or a parent's, needs the rule for each vaccine, not the leaflet's shorthand. Shingles adds a twist: eligibility turns on when a person turned 65, so two people of the same age can have different entitlements. The GOV.UK page for the 20-page PDF (5.04 MB) says general practitioners (GPs) should invite adults over 65 when they become eligible, that having vaccines when offered gives the best protection, and that some vaccines, such as flu, may also be available from community pharmacies. The flu program for adults 65 and over opened October 1, 2026 , and runs to March 31, 2027. Five Vaccines, Different Starting Rules Vaccine Who is eligible in England Schedule Source Flu Adults 65 and over (including those turning 65 by March 31, 2027), plus adults 18 to 64 with certain long-term conditions Annual NHS flu vaccine eligibility COVID-19 (autumn 2026) Adults 75 and over (including those turning 75 by January 31, 2027), older-adult care home residents, and people 6 months and over who are immunosuppressed Autumn campaign; online booking closes January 30, 2027 NHS winter vaccinations page RSV Everyone 75 and over, older-adult care home residents, and people 65 to 74 who are immunosuppressed or have chronic respiratory disease One dose (Abrysvo) UKHSA RSV clinician guidance Shingles People who turned 65 on or after September 1, 2023; people 70 to 79; severely immunosuppressed adults 18 and over Two doses (Shingrix) NHS shingles eligibility page Pneumococcal Adults 65 and over One dose NHS pneumococcal vaccine page COVID-19 Autumn Shot Skips Ages 65 to 74 Unless Immunosuppressed or in Care Homes Ministers accepted advice from the Joint Committee on Vaccination and Immunisation (JCVI), the expert panel that advises UK health ministries on vaccination, that the autumn 2026 program should focus on people at highest risk of serious disease. The government confirmed the groups on March 23, 2026. The listed groups do not include healthy adults 65 to 74, who qualify only if they are immunosuppressed or live in an older-adult care home. UKHSA surveillance data on last autumn's program showed vaccine effectiveness of 47% for the three months after vaccination. Eligible people can book online or in the NHS App without waiting for an invitation , online booking closes January 30, 2027, and the last vaccination date is January 31, 2027. The vaccine is usually offered no earlier than about six months after a previous COVID-19 dose. RSV Eligibility Moved Twice in 2026: Adults 80 and Over in April, At-Risk 65-to-74s in September Before April, the RSV program covered people turning 75 and a catch-up group aged 75 to 79. From April 1, 2026 , it extended to all adults 80 and over and all older-adult care home residents, which NHS England said brought in about 3 million more people. From September 1, 2026 , it widened to adults 65 to 74 with a weakened immune system or a long-term lung condition. UKHSA's clinician guidance on qualifying conditions lists COPD, cystic fibrosis, interstitial lung fibrosis, chronic obstructive bronchiectasis, pneumoconiosis and bronchopulmonary dysplasia among the lung conditions. Asthma counts only if poorly controlled, meaning two or more oral corticosteroid courses in the past 24 months, maintenance oral corticosteroids, or an asthma hospital admission in that period. The vaccine is one 0.5 ml (about 0.017 US fluid ounces) dose of Abrysvo, and no revaccination is currently recommended. People vaccinated at 65 to 74 should not be invited again at 75. Trial data show protection lasts at least 24 months from Abrysvo and Arexvy. Unlike flu, RSV vaccination is not seasonal: the program runs year-round, though vaccination before winter gives the greatest benefit. The stakes are measurable. UKHSA estimates RSV causes about 175,000 GP episodes a year among people 65 and over in the UK and 5,000 to 7,500 deaths each winter among older adults in England and Wales, most of them in people over 75. A UKHSA study cited by Age UK puts the vaccine at around 82% effective against hospital admission in people 75 to 79. Some community pharmacies in parts of England also offer the RSV vaccine, according to NHS England, which says to book through a GP practice or, for care home residents, through the care home. Abrysvo, Shingrix and Pneumococcal Conjugate Shots Use Three Different Immune Triggers Abrysvo is a non-live, bivalent recombinant vaccine. Genetic material encoding an RSV protein is inserted into manufactured cells, which produce the protein; it is purified and put in the vaccine. "Bivalent" means it carries proteins from RSV subgroups A and B, and "pre-F" means the protein is in the prefusion form of the F protein the virus uses to enter human cells. That design took decades. A 1960s formalin-inactivated RSV vaccine left some RSV-naive children sicker: about 80% were hospitalized versus 5% of controls, and two children died. A 2013 crystal structure study then showed how to stabilize the F protein, the basis of later vaccines. Shingrix is a recombinant subunit vaccine: a purified truncated glycoprotein E antigen of the varicella-zoster virus mixed with the AS01B adjuvant, a liposomal blend of MPL and the QS-21 saponin, given as two intramuscular doses. It reduced shingles by 91.3% in people over 70 in trial data (relative risk reduction), and protection lasts at least seven years. Pneumococcal vaccines split on how they recruit the immune system. Polysaccharide vaccine PPV23 covers 23 serotypes and produces a B-cell response without T-cell help , which is weaker in older adults. Conjugate vaccines bind those sugars to a carrier protein, recruiting helper T cells and forming memory B cells. The trade-off is that conjugates cover fewer serotypes than PPV23, and PCV20 (Prevenar 20) covers 20. Shingles Eligibility Depends on When You Turned 65, Not Only Current Age People who turned 65 on or after September 1, 2023, are eligible at 65 . People who turned 65 before that date become eligible at 70, and anyone 70 to 79 is eligible. The Shingrix For All program began on September 1, 2023. The cutoff means two 68-year-olds can differ: one born before September 1, 1958, turned 65 before the cutoff and waits until 70, while one born on or after that date is eligible now. Two doses are given 6 to 12 months apart. Eligibility continues until the 80th birthday, and the second dose can be given up to the 81st birthday. Severely immunosuppressed adults 18 and over get two doses 8 weeks to 6 months apart. Uptake is the concern. UKHSA says fewer than half of adults take up the free shingles vaccine in their first year of eligibility, and coverage among people turning 71 who had been eligible since turning 70 was 53.5%. Where Can Over-65s Get Each Vaccine, and Must They Wait for GP Invitation? For flu and COVID-19, no. The NHS says eligible people can book COVID-19 shots without waiting for an invitation , online or in the NHS App, and Age UK says the same applies to flu bookings. The NHS also lists pharmacies that offer the flu vaccine . For shingles, the NHS says anyone eligible who has not been contacted by their GP practice should contact it directly . Age UK advises older people unsure whether they have had pneumococcal or shingles shots to check with their GP practice . Pneumococcal vaccination is one dose, offered to adults 65 and over . UKHSA's visual guide lists Prevenar 20 with Pneumovax 23 as an alternative for over-65s only where locally available, while UKHSA's complete schedule lists Pneumovax 23 first and Prevenar 20 once PPV23 stock is exhausted, so asking the practice which product it uses is sensible. Flu has its own wrinkles this year. UKHSA says all three flu strains needed updating , which it calls unusual, most adults are offered vaccination from early October, which may be later than in previous years, and the vaccine type depends on age, so some sites may wait for stock. The vaccine is routinely offered up to December, and to March for people newly eligible. NHS England's 2026/27 target is 75% uptake among adults 65 and over, against a 74% baseline last winter. RSV Shot Should Not Routinely Share Appointment With Flu Shot UKHSA's clinician guidance says Abrysvo should not routinely be given at the same appointment as seasonal flu vaccine, because flu vaccination may reduce the response to the RSV vaccine. No specific gap is required, and they can be given together if the person is unlikely to return or needs immediate protection. RSV, shingles, COVID-19 and pneumococcal vaccines can be given together, preferably at separate sites. Web Summary Lists No Age Thresholds, Dates or Invitation Process The GOV.UK summary describes the leaflet as a guide to the vaccines offered to adults over 65 and when they are offered, but it gives no age thresholds, months or dates. It also does not say how GPs will invite people or what happens to eligible people who are not contacted. The thresholds in this article come from separate UKHSA and NHS pages, and the 20-page PDF may carry more detail per vaccine. Check Birth Month, Cohort and Conditions on NHS Booking Pages Before Assuming Coverage Flu and pneumococcal vaccines start at 65. Shingles starts at 65 for people who turned 65 on or after September 1, 2023, and at 70 for those who turned 65 earlier. COVID-19 and RSV start at 75 for most adults, with RSV also open from 65 to 74 for people with weakened immune systems or qualifying lung conditions, and COVID-19 open earlier only to immunosuppressed people and care home residents. A parent or relative who assumes the "over 65" label means every shot is available now can miss the ones that are, or wait for ones that are not. The NHS booking pages and the GP practice are where to confirm coverage for each vaccine. Frequently Asked Questions Can a healthy 66-year-old get the COVID-19 vaccine in England this autumn? Not unless they are immunosuppressed or live in an older-adult care home. The program covers adults 75 and over, including those turning 75 by January 31, 2027, plus people 6 months and over who are immunosuppressed. Who can get the RSV vaccine in England? Everyone 75 and over, older-adult care home residents, and people 65 to 74 who are immunosuppressed or have a long-term lung condition such as COPD or poorly controlled asthma. It is a single dose, and well-controlled asthma does not qualify . Do I need to wait for an invitation to get a flu or COVID-19 vaccine? No. Eligible people can book flu and COVID-19 vaccination online or in the NHS App, and flu booking closes March 30, 2027 . Why can two people the same age have different shingles eligibility? Shingles eligibility depends on when a person turned 65. Those who turned 65 on or after September 1, 2023, are eligible at 65, while those who turned 65 before that date become eligible at 70, so two 68-year-olds can be treated differently depending on their birth date. c 2026 TECHTIMES.com All rights reserved. records.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Culture – Society Y tế Experts discuss measures to prevent RSV in young children. Protecting the respiratory health of newborns and infants requires preparation from the mother's pregnancy until after the child is born; this involves coordination between obstetricians, pediatricians, and the family. Báo Nhân dân•21/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Overview of the scientific conference. (Photo: LE HUYEN) The Center for Training Healthcare Human Resources to Meet Social Needs, under the Ho Chi Minh City University of Medicine and Pharmacy, and Pfizer Vietnam recently collaborated to organize a scientific workshop titled “United for the First Breath – Working Together to Protect the First Breath of Life,” bringing together approximately 150 experts from the Asian region. At the workshop, experts focused on discussing the burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants, especially in the first few months of life, while emphasizing the role of preventive measures starting from pregnancy. Tìm hiểu lịch sử Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the most common causes of lower respiratory tract infections in young children. Notably, younger children are at higher risk of hospitalization due to RSV. A meta-analysis of data from 61 studies in 19 countries showed that the highest rate of RSV-related hospitalizations was in children aged 0 to under 3 months, and then decreased with age. Khám phá thêm Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch Khám phá ĐNA Đọc Tin Tức Dr. Phan Huu Phuc, MD, PhD, speaking at the conference. (Photo: LE HUYEN) Research data from the National Children's Hospital shows that among children hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis, 42.7% are under 3 months old. Analysis based on data from Children's Hospital 1 ( Ho Chi Minh City) estimates that approximately 25% of severe RSV cases requiring hospitalization in children under 5 years old occur in the under-3-month age group. In northern Japan, hospitalizations for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis occur year-round and tend to increase between October and March. In southern Japan, RSV season typically coincides with the rainy season, from approximately May to November each year. You may also like Currently, there is no specific treatment for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), so treatment mainly focuses on symptom control and respiratory support. In severe cases, children may need hospitalization, even in an intensive care unit, and require respiratory support measures, including invasive mechanical ventilation. In particularly severe cases, children may need extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Besides the risk of severe complications during the acute phase, even after recovery from respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections, there can still be long-term effects on a child's respiratory health. Several observational studies have shown that children who have had lower respiratory tract infections caused by RSV in their early years have a higher risk of recurrent wheezing and asthma later in life. Dr. Phan Huu Phuc, Deputy Director of the National Children's Hospital and Secretary General of the Vietnam Pediatric Association, pointed out that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the common causes of bronchiolitis and pneumonia in newborns and young children. RSV-induced bronchiolitis can progress to severe lower respiratory tract infections, even life-threatening ones, requiring hospitalization and mechanical ventilation. The first few months of life are a critical period for children and require special attention from their families. Children under 3 months old hospitalized with RSV have a much higher risk of needing respiratory support than older children. Therefore, in addition to monitoring their child's health after birth, parents should proactively learn about RSV and discuss it with their doctor during pregnancy, especially if the expected delivery date falls during months when RSV is more prevalent. Tìm hiểu lịch sử Given the risk of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants during their first few months of life, experts emphasize that protecting children's respiratory health should not only begin when symptoms appear, but should also be considered from the prenatal stage. During pregnancy, the mother's body not only nourishes the developing fetus but also contributes to shaping the immune foundation for the child after birth. Associate Professor, Dr. Huynh Nguyen Khanh Trang speaks at the conference. (Photo: LE HUYEN) Associate Professor, Dr. Huynh Nguyen Khanh Trang, Head of the Obstetrics and Gynecology Department, Pham Ngoc Thach University of Medicine; Head of the Obstetrics Department - Head of the Obstetrics Unit, Hung Vuong Hospital, shared: In obstetric practice, a child's health doesn't begin with their first cry, but is shaped during pregnancy. Pregnancy is the "window of opportunity" for mothers to prepare a protective foundation for their children from the very first days - the period when the child's immune system is still immature and most vulnerable to agents such as respiratory syncytial virus. The role of an obstetrician is not only to monitor a healthy pregnancy, but also to be a companion, providing reliable scientific information and working with the family to prepare for the child's ongoing care. You may also like Based on scientific evidence and practical experience shared at the workshop, experts emphasized the collaborative role of obstetricians and pediatricians in helping parents access accurate information throughout pregnancy and postpartum. With the advantage of accompanying pregnant women during routine check-ups, obstetricians can be the starting point for parents to learn about respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), identify risks, and discuss appropriate preventive measures. After the child is born, pediatricians continue to support families in recognizing signs of the disease, monitoring respiratory health, and choosing appropriate care for the child. Biologically, antibodies transferred from mother to child through the placenta gradually increase with gestational age and reach approximately 50% of the mother's concentration by week 32, demonstrating that pregnancy is a foundational period for preparing the child's respiratory system. Therefore, experts emphasize the seamless integration between the two specialties, ensuring uninterrupted respiratory care for children. Quang Minh Source: Báo Nhân dân Original articleCopy https://nhandan.vn/chuyen-gia-thao-luan-cac-bien-phap-du-phong-rsv-doi-voi-tre-nho-post1004481.html Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Comment (0) Top Interests Newest Please leave a comment to share your feelings! Nov 19, 2026 7:00 AM Share on SPACES Share by Email Share on Facebook Share on X Share on LinkedIn Print Share via Text Message Listen to this article 00:03:29 As colder weather arrives, many people are thinking about their flu and COVID-19 vaccines. Another respiratory virus, known as RSV, also deserves attention, particularly among older adults. Respiratory syncytial virus often causes symptoms similar to a cold. But for older adults and people with certain health conditions, it can lead to pneumonia and hospitalization. “People often associate RSV with babies and young children,” says Richard Procunier, pharmacist and owner of Northern Shores Pharmacy in North Bay. “Older adults should know about it too, especially if they’re already managing health conditions that make respiratory infections harder on them.” Who should consider vaccination? Canada’s National Advisory Committee on Immunization recommends RSV vaccination for everyone aged 75 and older, and adults aged 65 to 74 at increased risk of serious illness. Certain younger adults with particularly high-risk conditions are also recommended to receive it. Chronic lung disease, heart disease, diabetes and a weakened immune system can increase the risk of severe RSV. A pharmacist can help you understand how your age and health history affect the recommendation. “The decision should reflect your individual health,” Procunier explains. “A conversation with your pharmacist can help you understand your risk and whether this vaccine would be a useful part of your protection.” How can your pharmacy help? Pharmacies that offer RSV vaccination can dispense the vaccine and administer the injection. For a privately purchased dose, you need a prescription from your doctor or nurse practitioner. If your doctor’s office cannot provide the injection, it can be arranged at the pharmacy. “Call us first,” Procunier says. “We can review your vaccination history, answer questions and explain what you need to arrange an appointment.” Ontario provides free doses to everyone aged 75 and older and certain eligible adults aged 60 to 74, but publicly funded RSV vaccines are not currently available through community pharmacies. Eligible patients should contact their primary care provider or the North Bay Parry Sound District Health Unit. For private pharmacy vaccination, insurance may cover some or all of the cost; check before purchasing, as Ontario does not reimburse private purchases. Is it another yearly shot? RSV vaccination is not currently an annual vaccination. A single adult dose provides protection for several years, and routine repeat doses are not presently recommended. Adults can receive it at the same visit as their flu and COVID-19 vaccines when appropriate. Common side effects include a sore arm, tiredness, headache and muscle aches. Your pharmacist can explain expected reactions and discuss rare risks alongside the benefits. “You don’t have to figure out your vaccination needs on your own,” Procunier says. “Bring your questions to the team at Northern Shores Pharmacy. We can help you make an informed decision and take the next step." Learn more at the Northern Shores Pharmacy in North Bay. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (WBTV) - Three major health care systems based in the Charlotte region were implementing visitor restrictions at medical facilities to limit the spread of viruses as the holidays near. Charlotte-based Atrium Health and Winston-Salem-based Novant Health announced this week that temporary visitor restrictions would take effect on Thursday, Nov. 19. On Friday, Gastonia-based CaroMont Health said that visitor restrictions would take effect at three hospitals starting next week. The health systems each said the restrictions were meant to limit the spread of viruses as cases of the flu, COVID-19 and RSV increase in the region. It is common for health care systems to establish temporary visitor restrictions during the colder months. records.content: 污水源病原病毒在河口与近海环境中的归趋:整合实验-模型框架的病毒扩散、衰变与暴露风险量化研究 《One Health》:The fate of wastewater-derived pathogenic viruses in estuarine and coastal waters 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月24日 来源:One Health 5.3 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 污水源病毒普遍存在于河流、河口与近海环境中,可能对人类健康构成严重风险。然而,由于复杂的水动力过程与病毒特异性行为,其环境归趋难以预测。本研究旨在构建一个整合实验与模型的框架,以量化病毒在河-河口-近海连续体(river-estuary-coastal continuum)中的扩散、衰变与暴露风险。研究人员在受控微宇宙(microcosm)实验中,于不同温度、盐度与紫外(ultraviolet, UV)辐射条件下推导了五种人类病原病毒(诺如病毒替代株(以HAV作为NoV替代株)、腺病毒(Adenovirus)、非脊髓灰质炎肠道病毒(Non-polio Enterovirus)、甲型流感病毒(Influenza-A virus)与呼吸道合胞病毒(Respiratory Syncytial Virus))的病毒特异性衰变函数。平均T90衰变时间尺度从9天(甲型流感病毒)到41天(诺如病毒)不等。随后,研究人员将这些衰变函数嵌入英国康威河口(Conwy estuary)的水动力-水质耦合模型(Delft3D)中。模型性能依据病毒浓度的现场观测进行了评估。模型敏感性测试与基于真实事件的模拟(涵盖当代及预测的未来气候情景)表明,病毒的归趋取决于病毒载量、下游河流输运、河口停留时间(residence time)与病毒特异性衰变的共同作用。停留时间与衰变时间尺度之间的平衡对暴露风险具有重要影响:在最坏情景下,具有感染性的诺如病毒水平可在河口持续存在长达12天。在决定暴露风险时,病毒载量超过了病毒固有衰变特性的影响。UV辐射是病毒衰变的主控因子,而水温和盐度的影响相对较弱(甲型流感病毒除外)。寒冷湿润条件因病毒载量高且光灭活(photoinactivation)程度最低,造成最大的暴露风险;然而值得注意的是,在极强河流流量情景下风险反而下降,因为病毒在河口内的停留时间最短,被快速冲刷至近海。而在温暖晴朗条件下(相同病毒载量,分别为5.3320e+08、6.0413e+07、1.1513e+07、3.6525e+06、1.7302e+06 gc s?1,对应诺如病毒替代株、腺病毒、非脊髓灰质炎肠道病毒、甲型流感病毒与呼吸道合胞病毒),病毒衰变增强,因而暴露风险明显降低。预测的21世纪气候变暖以及海平面上升引起的停留时间缩短,未来可能降低河口内的病毒暴露风险。该框架将实验室推导的病毒衰变行为与基于过程的水动力模拟相联系,可支持基于特定场址的感染风险评估与气候适应型水质管理。 研究背景 欢迎领取《抗体药研发解决方案》 领 取 生活污水排入河流、湖泊与近海水体,构成多种人类病原病毒的传播节点,威胁游泳者健康并影响水产养殖与旅游业。风险既来自部分处理废水的持续排放,也来自未经处理的污水(合流制溢流,combined sewage overflows, CSOs)的间歇排放,相关健康效应包括急性胃肠炎、呼吸系统疾病与肝功能损害,其中诺如病毒是疾病暴发的最大单一病因。随着人口增长与降水和径流事件更趋频繁强烈,CSOs排放可能增加,该问题预计进一步恶化。然而,由于采样有限与水质建模不足,相关风险仍缺乏量化。关键不确定性包括:不同病毒在预测变暖的水温、更强的高浊度洪水、更强更长的紫外(ultraviolet, UV)辐射以及海平面上升作用下将如何衰变;病毒的个体与联合效应在预测水质模型中表征不足。水文水动力过程决定病毒在数天至数周活性期间的分布与浓度,潮汐振荡控制其在河口的停留时间。未来气候变化预计改变上述控制,海平面上升(预计2100年上升0.3–1.0 m)将进一步缩短河口停留时间,人为影响也将改变相关公共健康风险。 研究开展、结论与意义 研究人员(Xiaorong Li、Thomas Clough、Jessica Kevill、Nia Jones、Shelagh K. Malham、Davey L. Jones、Peter Robins)在英国北威尔士康威河口(Conwy estuary)开展了整合受控微宇宙实验与过程驱动水动力-水质建模的研究,旨在量化病毒在河-河口-近海连续体(river-estuary-coastal continuum)中的扩散、衰变与暴露风险。主要结论为:河流流量、病毒载量与河口停留时间共同控制病毒归趋;UV辐射是衰变的主控因子;在河口尺度上病毒载量对暴露风险的控制作用强于固有衰变特性;寒冷湿润条件产生最大暴露风险;未来变暖与海平面上升可能降低河口病毒暴露风险。该框架将实验室推导的病毒衰变行为与基于过程的水动力模拟相联系,支持基于特定场址的感染风险评估与气候适应型水质管理,并可为细菌与真菌等其他病原体提供可迁移的方法。 主要关键技术方法 关键技术方法包括:受控微宇宙实验(在康威河流域淡水、半咸水、海水三类水样中研究温度、盐度与模拟日光(UV辐射)的影响,用qPCR(定量聚合酶链式反应)与CI-qPCR(衣壳完整性qPCR)定量病毒并推导T90衰变时间);衰变方程构建(基于Delft3D内置衰变方程适配);水动力建模(Delft3D D-Flow Flexible Mesh模块,8个天文分潮驱动);水质建模(D-Water Quality模块,病毒作为可衰减示踪剂);现场验证采样(2025年3月于康威河与河口Llanrwst、Treffriw、Tal-y-Cafn三处位点采样,结合Betws-y-Coed与Llanrwst两座污水处理厂(WwTW)排放数据验证)。 研究结果 3.1 病毒衰变曲线与衰变系数 通过曲线拟合确定五种病毒的衰变系数:衰变率与氯化物浓度(盐度)呈线性关系、与水温呈指数关系、与UV辐射呈线性关系。平均T90衰变时间从9天(甲型流感病毒)到41天(诺如病毒)不等,在最小衰变条件(盐度0 ppt、温度11 °C、UV 0.72 W m?2)下最长。 3.2 模型验证 水动力模型能良好复现潮位与流速(Llandudno潮位站NRMSE=3%),盐度与16个站点观测一致;水质模型基本能模拟三个采样点的观测浓度,如Llanrwst处肠道病毒模拟与观测相关系数r=0.86、诺如病毒GII r=0.67、诺如病毒GI r=0.71,平均浓度总体接近。病毒浓度呈现潮汐驱动的重复振荡模式。 3.3 敏感性情景1–4下的病毒扩散与衰变 90个敏感性模拟显示病毒浓度随向下游距离呈反S型下降(p<0.001)。河流流量是病毒扩散的主控因子(ANOVA F=15.1–16.9,p<0.01):低流量(10百分位0.9 m3 s?1)下停留时间数天,病毒主要于上半河口衰变;高流量(95百分位)下停留时间缩短至1天以内,病毒可输出河口。UV辐射是衰变的主控因子(F=3.9–6.0,p<0.01),而水温与盐度总体仅产生细微且不显著的差异(p>0.85),仅甲型流感病毒表现出盐度与衰变的正相关。基于100 gc l?1参考浓度,腺病毒风险最高、甲型流感病毒最低,呼吸道合胞病毒未达阈值。 3.4 事件情景1–3下的病毒持久性与河口恢复 事件情景1(冬季风暴)为最坏情景:大部分河口与邻近Conwy湾水域在分析期10–90%的时间内超过参考浓度;1天强风暴情景下河口超过参考浓度的比例高达99.6%,河口平均约2天、最长7.5天恢复至安全水平;3天与5天风暴情景下该比例分别达99.8%与99.9%,平均恢复时间约3.3–3.5天、最长10.9–11.3天。值得注意的是,1天强风暴(峰值流量超700 m3 s?1)比3天、5天弱风暴风险更低,因其将病毒快速冲刷至近海稀释。事件情景2(夏季"海滩日")因高温与UV增强使衰变加快,暴露风险降低(超过概率最高23.7%–62%,恢复时间最长5–9天),但恰逢游泳高峰。事件情景3(未来"海滩日")显示2100年变暖与海平面上升进一步缩短风险持续时间(超过概率最高23.5%–58.4%,恢复时间最长3–7天)。线性混合效应模型表明情景对恢复时间有显著影响(F(2, 36)=5.27),而风暴持续时间无显著主效应。 讨论部分 讨论指出,潮汐主导的河口通过振荡潮汐通量对病毒形成强缓冲,限制其向近海的输送;河川径流流量在很大程度上控制病毒向下游输运的范围,低流量下病毒滞留数天,衰变动力学直接决定暴露风险。尽管固有衰变速率排序为IAV>RSV>EV>HAdV>NoV,模拟暴露风险排序为HAdV>EV>NoV>IAV>RSV,与观测病毒载量一致,表明在河口尺度上病毒载量对浓度的控制作用强于固有衰变特性,但平均载量法可能低估高载量事件的尾部风险。局限性包括:病毒载量仅从河口上游单点输入,未纳入多点源;未考虑病毒与悬浮颗粒物、沉积物的相互作用;未考虑水生生物群落的影响;HAV作为NoV替代株,其抗性更强,所得T90可能为保守估计;以100 gc l?1基因拷贝基准定义风险,不等同于感染风险比较。 结论 本研究提出了一个整合实验与模型的框架,以改善对河-河口-海系统中污水源病毒污染及相关健康风险的预测。在病毒释放后的最初数天内,河流流量、病毒载量与河口停留时间控制病毒的归趋与暴露风险;在滞留数天的河口条件下,病毒衰变行为对暴露风险起决定作用,对UV辐射高度敏感,对水温和盐度的敏感度较低。基于事件的模拟揭示了病毒暴露风险强烈的季节与气候调节:冬季风暴情景因灭活作用最小而产生最大环境风险,夏季情景病毒暴露减少但与娱乐性水体接触高峰重合。未来气候情景表明,增强的衰变与海平面上升引起的河口冲刷将缩短参考浓度水平的持续时间。 Jones、Peter Robins)在英国北威尔士康威河口(Conwy estuary)开展了整合受控微宇宙实验与过程驱动水动力-水质建模的研究,旨在量化病毒在河-河口-近海连续体(river-estuary-coastal continuum)中的扩散、衰变与暴露风险。主要结论为:河流流量、病毒载量与河口停留时间共同控制病毒归趋;UV辐射是衰变的主控因子;在河口尺度上病毒载量对暴露风险的控制作用强于固有衰变特性;寒冷湿润条件产生最大暴露风险;未来变暖与海平面上升可能降低河口病毒暴露风险。该框架将实验室推导的病毒衰变行为与基于过程的水动力模拟相联系,支持基于特定场址的感染风险评估与气候适应型水质管理,并可为细菌与真菌等其他病原体提供可迁移的方法。主要关键技术方法关键技术方法包括:受控微宇宙实验(在康威河流域淡水、半咸水、海水三类水样中研究温度、盐度与模拟日光(UV辐射)的影响,用qPCR(定量聚合酶链式反应)与CI-qPCR(衣壳完整性qPCR)定量病毒并推导T90衰变时间);衰变方程构建(基于Delft3D内置衰变方程适配);水动力建模(Delft3D D-Flow Flexible Mesh模块,8个天文分潮驱动);水质建模(D-Water Quality模块,病毒作为可衰减示踪剂);现场验证采样(2025年3月于康威河与河口Llanrwst、Treffriw、Tal-y-Cafn三处位点采样,结合Betws-y-Coed与Llanrwst两座污水处理厂(WwTW)排放数据验证)。研究结果3.1 病毒衰变曲线与衰变系数通过曲线拟合确定五种病毒的衰变系数:衰变率与氯化物浓度(盐度)呈线性关系、与水温呈指数关系、与UV辐射呈线性关系。平均T90衰变时间从9天(甲型流感病毒)到41天(诺如病毒)不等,在最小衰变条件(盐度0 ppt、温度11 °C、UV 0.72 W m)下最长。3.2 模型验证水动力模型能良好复现潮位与流速(Llandudno潮位站NRMSE=3%),盐度与16个站点观测一致;水质模型基本能模拟三个采样点的观测浓度,如Llanrwst处肠道病毒模拟与观测相关系数r=0.86、诺如病毒GII r=0.67、诺如病毒GI r=0.71,平均浓度总体接近。病毒浓度呈现潮汐驱动的重复振荡模式。3.3 敏感性情景1–4下的病毒扩散与衰变90个敏感性模拟显示病毒浓度随向下游距离呈反S型下降(p<0.001)。河流流量是病毒扩散的主控因子(ANOVA F=15.1–16.9,p<0.01):低流量(10百分位0.9 m)下停留时间数天,病毒主要于上半河口衰变;高流量(95百分位)下停留时间缩短至1天以内,病毒可输出河口。UV辐射是衰变的主控因子(F=3.9–6.0,p<0.01),而水温与盐度总体仅产生细微且不显著的差异(p>0.85),仅甲型流感病毒表现出盐度与衰变的正相关。基于100 gc l参考浓度,腺病毒风险最高、甲型流感病毒最低,呼吸道合胞病毒未达阈值。3.4 事件情景1–3下的病毒持久性与河口恢复事件情景1(冬季风暴)为最坏情景:大部分河口与邻近Conwy湾水域在分析期10–90%的时间内超过参考浓度;1天强风暴情景下河口超过参考浓度的比例高达99.6%,河口平均约2天、最长7.5天恢复至安全水平;3天与5天风暴情景下该比例分别达99.8%与99.9%,平均恢复时间约3.3–3.5天、最长10.9–11.3天。值得注意的是,1天强风暴(峰值流量超700 m)比3天、5天弱风暴风险更低,因其将病毒快速冲刷至近海稀释。事件情景2(夏季"海滩日")因高温与UV增强使衰变加快,暴露风险降低(超过概率最高23.7%–62%,恢复时间最长5–9天),但恰逢游泳高峰。事件情景3(未来"海滩日")显示2100年变暖与海平面上升进一步缩短风险持续时间(超过概率最高23.5%–58.4%,恢复时间最长3–7天)。线性混合效应模型表明情景对恢复时间有显著影响(F(2, 36)=5.27),而风暴持续时间无显著主效应。讨论部分讨论指出,潮汐主导的河口通过振荡潮汐通量对病毒形成强缓冲,限制其向近海的输送;河川径流流量在很大程度上控制病毒向下游输运的范围,低流量下病毒滞留数天,衰变动力学直接决定暴露风险。尽管固有衰变速率排序为IAV>RSV>EV>HAdV>NoV,模拟暴露风险排序为HAdV>EV>NoV>IAV>RSV,与观测病毒载量一致,表明在河口尺度上病毒载量对浓度的控制作用强于固有衰变特性,但平均载量法可能低估高载量事件的尾部风险。局限性包括:病毒载量仅从河口上游单点输入,未纳入多点源;未考虑病毒与悬浮颗粒物、沉积物的相互作用;未考虑水生生物群落的影响;HAV作为NoV替代株,其抗性更强,所得T90可能为保守估计;以100 gc l基因拷贝基准定义风险,不等同于感染风险比较。结论本研究提出了一个整合实验与模型的框架,以改善对河-河口-海系统中污水源病毒污染及相关健康风险的预测。在病毒释放后的最初数天内,河流流量、病毒载量与河口停留时间控制病毒的归趋与暴露风险;在滞留数天的河口条件下,病毒衰变行为对暴露风险起决定作用,对UV辐射高度敏感,对水温和盐度的敏感度较低。基于事件的模拟揭示了病毒暴露风险强烈的季节与气候调节:冬季风暴情景因灭活作用最小而产生最大环境风险,夏季情景病毒暴露减少但与娱乐性水体接触高峰重合。未来气候情景表明,增强的衰变与海平面上升引起的河口冲刷将缩短参考浓度水平的持续时间。 records.content: 虎嗅APP虎嗅APP 公众号矩阵公众号矩阵 虎嗅APP AGI接口 商业弧光 那个NG 妙投APP 出海潜望 智库 加入社群加入社群 AI硬件社群 AI原生社群 智库AI创新落地交流群 妙投行研投资交流群 早点生活交流群 我要投稿我要投稿 资讯 24小时 源流 视频 虎嗅视界 视频精选 活动/榜单/专题 妙投 虎嗅智库 虎嗅嗅全新升级虎嗅嗅全新升级 文章 作者 相关度 最新 **三叶草生物市值三年涨约91.8%至17.4亿港元,但2026上半年营收仅17.9万元,净利9.55亿元主要靠Gavi和解收益,RSV管线支撑估值修复。** **要点** **1. 市值低位修复但仍远低于发行价** 市值由2023年11月约9.07亿港元升至2026年11月17.4亿港元,涨约91.8%;但较13.38港元发行价低约90%,较上市首日150亿港元缩水超8成。 **2. 净利扭亏主要来自Gavi和解一次性收益** 2026上半年营收17.9万元、同比降94.5%,净利9.55亿元;Gavi和解带来约10.87亿元一次性收益,剔除后亏1.32亿元。 **3. 经营现金流与持续经营压力突出** 上半年经营现金净流出1.80亿元,6月底现金约9054万元,低于2025年底2.71亿元;中报提示持续经营重大不确定性。 **4. RSV联合疫苗进展积极但商业化待验证** SCB-1022/1033 II期初步显示RSV、hMPV中和抗体提升6至9倍;SCB-1019重复接种有早期积极信号。但样本有限,面临GSK、辉瑞、Moderna竞争,商业化待验证。 2026-11-23 02:50 三年市值涨超90%,三叶草生物迎来新转机?|市值观察 医线Insight关注 速览 三叶草生物市值三年涨约91.8%至17.4亿港元,但2026上半年营收仅17.9万元,净利9.55亿元主要靠Gavi和解收益,RSV管线支撑估值修复。 展开更多 本文来自微信公众号: 医线Insight ,制图:医线Insight,作者:雨山,原文标题:《三年市值涨超90%,三叶草生物迎来新转机?|市值观察》 一家半年营收只有17.9万元的疫苗公司,资本市场愿意给出多少估值? 三叶草生物的最新市值,给出了答案:17.4亿港元——2026年11月20日收盘,三叶草生物股价为1.34港元,总市值约17.4亿港元。 以2023年11月约0.70港元的基准股价和同期总股本估算,公司市值从约9.07亿港元升至17.4亿港元,累计增长约91.8%,是三年前的1.92倍。 若与上市之初相比,这轮上涨仍属于低位修复。 2021年11月,三叶草生物以13.38港元的发行价登陆港交所,上市首日市值约150亿港元。五年过去,股价较发行价仍低约90%,市值也较上市首日缩水超过8成。 财报呈现的情况,同样值得关注。 2026年上半年,公司营业收入仅17.9万元人民币,同比下降约94.5%;净利润却达到9.55亿元人民币,实现大幅扭亏。 过去几年,公司先后经历了新冠疫苗需求退潮、AdimFlu-S在中国大陆的商业化合作终止,以及涉及2.24亿美元预付款的Gavi合同争议。 眼下,更值得关注的变化出现在研发端:公司正把资源集中到呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)及多病毒联合疫苗,希望借助新的产品管线打开增长空间。 市值回暖、账面扭亏、研发提速,几方面的变化放在一起看,三叶草生物似乎正在迎来新的发展契机。 01 市场重新为未来定价 要看懂这一轮市值回升,还得从2021年说起。 当时全球新冠疫苗需求旺盛,疫苗研发、产能建设和国际采购协议,都是资本市场关注生物医药企业的重要看点。 2021年11月5日,三叶草生物在港交所挂牌,发行价13.38港元,全球发售1.5亿股;根据公司2023年年报,全球发售所得款项净额约为18.84亿港元。 尽管上市首日跌破发行价,以12.98港元收盘,公司市值仍达到约150.32亿港元。 彼时,市场看重的不只是新冠疫苗,还有Trimer-Tag蛋白质三聚体化技术平台,以及公司在更多创新疫苗品种上的研发潜力。 作为一家疫苗Biotech,三叶草生物既要证明自己的临床研发能力,也要依靠生产设施和国际合作,把研发成果转化为商业收入。 但此后几年,市场环境发生了明显变化。 随着新冠疫苗需求回落,原先支撑高估值的市场空间迅速收窄。对于尚未建立稳定商业收入的疫苗公司,研发投入与盈利之间的落差更加突出,三叶草生物的股价也持续承压。 2023年10月19日,三叶草生物股价一度跌至0.57港元,2024年又长期处于低位。 第三方历史月度行情显示,2025年4月,其月度股价甚至只有约0.21港元。从13.38港元的发行价跌至不足0.3港元,市场对公司的估值经历了一次深度调整。 如今,市场重新把目光投向三叶草生物,并非没有原因。 公司在经营层面和研发端都出现了实质性变化。 2026年3月,Gavi合同争议达成和解,一项悬而未决的历史问题得到处理;与此同时,以RSV为核心的创新疫苗管线也接连取得进展。 2026年1月,公司宣布在澳大利亚启动RSV+hMPV±PIV3呼吸道联合疫苗II期临床试验;3月披露RSV疫苗重复接种研究的新数据;9月再公布联合疫苗II期临床的积极初步结果。 这些变化为市场重新评估三叶草生物提供了依据。过去三年市值明显回升,也反映出投资者开始重新关注公司的长期研发价值。 当然,从估值修复到形成稳定的经营循环,还需要继续拿出成果。 但与此前相比,公司已具备更清晰的发力方向。 02 盈利真相 在重新赢得资本市场关注之前,三叶草生物已经历过两次商业化考验:一次是新冠疫苗,一次是流感疫苗。 2022年12月,公司自主研发的重组蛋白新冠疫苗SCB-2019获得中国紧急使用授权。 2023年2月,公司开始在中国多个省市推进商业化,但市场窗口已不同于疫情高峰期。 公司在2023年年报中坦言,当时市场主要依赖政府采购,受市场准入机会有限、接种需求偏低影响,中国新冠疫苗市场的商业价值相当有限。 疫苗销售还受接种政策、采购体系、公众意愿和竞争格局影响。公共卫生事件带动的需求变化可能快于研发周期,产品完成临床开发时,商业机会或已收窄。 为培育新收入,2023年2月,三叶草生物与国光生技签署独家合作协议,取得AdimFlu-S四价流感疫苗在中国大陆的商业化权益;同年9月,产品上市。 根据2023年年报,该产品已进入28个省级行政区域的准入体系,并于当年11月完成巴西上市申报。公司希望借此积累销售经验、搭建渠道并更快获得收入,但业务表现未达预期。 2023年,三叶草生物营业收入3925.5万元人民币,销售及分销开支5476.6万元。二者不能反映单款疫苗利润,但显示初期市场开发投入不小。 2024年,公司全年收入3841.9万元;2025年降至350.5万元,主要来自此前产品实际退货率低于预估而作出的调整,并非持续销售规模。 2025年6月,公司终止与国光生技的合作,不再在中国大陆分销AdimFlu-S,称合作终止缘于市场环境发生重大变化,不会对集团经营造成重大不利影响。 至此,引进成熟流感疫苗建立稳定收入来源的尝试暂告一段落。 2026年上半年,公司营业收入进一步降至17.9万元,产品销售尚不足以支撑整体经营。 新冠疫苗业务留下的财务影响仍需消化。2023年,公司对主要涉及原材料的存货计提约16.97亿元人民币拨备;2024年又因新冠疫苗相关原材料计提大额减值,全年亏损约9.03亿元人民币。需求变化后,前期供应链投入未必能迅速转作他用。 另一项历史问题来自Gavi合同。 2021年6月,三叶草生物与全球疫苗免疫联盟Gavi签署新冠疫苗预购协议:Gavi计划采购6400万剂疫苗,并可选择进一步采购最多3.5亿剂;公司获得2.24亿美元预付款。 此后双方产生合同争议。2025年,Gavi要求退还预付款并申请仲裁。 2026年3月22日,双方达成和解:三叶草生物需支付700万美元前期现金款项,并承担上限2200万美元的递延付款,以及上限3600万美元、与未来收入和融资等挂钩的或有付款,相关安排涉及最长12年的协议期限。 2026年中报显示,终止确认原有合同负债并确认未来预计支付义务,带来约10.87亿元人民币的一次性收益。 上半年净利润约9.55亿元;剔除后仍亏损约1.32亿元人民币,该数字也见于持续经营相关附注。近10亿元净利润并非疫苗销售盈利。 和解不意味着付款义务全部消除。截至2026年6月底,公司账面仍确认约3.95亿元人民币的Gavi和解应付款项;与Dynavax、CEPI有关的历史佐剂采购安排,也对应一定规模的应付款项。 现金流压力同样存在。 2026年上半年,经营活动现金净流出约1.80亿元人民币,研发费用约1.05亿元。截至2026年6月底,现金及银行结余约9054万元,低于2025年底的2.71亿元;集团负债净额约8.01亿元。 中报称持续经营能力仍存在重大不确定性,公司拟调整研发优先顺序、控制开支、寻求融资和全球合作;管理层仍认为按持续经营基础编制财务报表是适当的。 2023年,约25.41亿元人民币的CEPI资助在满足相关条件后被确认为其他收入及收益。 这类非主营业务会计项目与Gavi和解收益性质不同,评价公司仍需关注管线进度、资金状况和持续经营能力,不能只看净利润。 Gavi争议达成和解,是三叶草生物化解历史不确定性的重要一步。 旧问题逐步厘清后,下一步重点便是如何培育能够支撑公司长期发展的新收入来源。 03 RSV打开新的增长想象空间 在三叶草生物的新一轮研发布局中,RSV是最值得关注的方向。 RSV即呼吸道合胞病毒,是常见的重要呼吸道病原体之一,对老年人、婴幼儿以及部分有基础疾病的人群,可能造成严重健康风险。 随着全球人口老龄化和疾病预防需求增加,RSV疫苗成为备受关注的研发方向。 这一领域已有实力雄厚的竞争者。 2023年,GSK和辉瑞的成人RSV疫苗先后获得美国监管批准;2024年,Moderna的mResvia也在美国获批。 截至2026年,美国已有三款获许可的成人RSV疫苗:GSK的Arexvy、辉瑞的Abrysvo和Moderna的mResvia。 跨国药企在产品上市、临床证据和商业渠道上已经抢占先机。 对后来者而言,仅证明疫苗能够诱导免疫反应还不够,必须拿出自己的产品特点。 三叶草生物选择的突破方向,正是差异化。 目前,公司重点推进三款相关候选疫苗。其中,SCB-1019是一款RSV候选疫苗,着重研究老年人群的免疫应答,并探索已接种其他RSV疫苗的人群再次接种的可能性。 SCB-1022则把RSV与人偏肺病毒(hMPV)结合,开发能够同时针对两种病原体的呼吸道二联疫苗。 SCB-1033在此基础上加入副流感病毒3型(PIV3),尝试用一款三联疫苗覆盖三种呼吸道病原体。 与单一病原体疫苗相比,联合疫苗有望覆盖更多呼吸道病毒,也能让预防接种更加便利。 对于已经接种过RSV疫苗的老年人,如果再次接种既能恢复RSV保护,又能增加对其他病毒的保护,就可能形成具有吸引力的新应用场景。 当然,这需要临床证据和接种政策的共同支持。 按照美国CDC目前的成人RSV疫苗接种建议,75岁及以上成年人,以及50至74岁具有较高重症风险的人群,建议接种一剂RSV疫苗。 现阶段,RSV疫苗不是每年常规重复接种的疫苗;对已经接种过的人群,CDC目前也不建议常规追加剂次。 因此,重复接种市场还不能简单按照成熟的年度疫苗市场估算。三叶草生物仍需用临床数据验证再次接种的价值,并关注未来接种建议是否调整。 也正因如此,谁能率先拿出有说服力的证据,谁就更有机会在这一新场景中建立优势。 从近期数据看,公司已取得一些值得关注的进展。 2026年3月,三叶草生物披露一项美国I期临床试验数据。研究纳入此前至少两个流行季前接种过GSK Arexvy疫苗的60至85岁老年人,比较再次接种SCB-1019、Arexvy和安慰剂后的免疫应答。 公司公布的62名受试者探索性分析显示,SCB-1019组的RSV-A和RSV-B中和抗体几何平均滴度,呈现较Arexvy重复接种组高约60%至80%的趋势。 对探索重复接种差异化而言,这是一个积极的早期信号。 需要注意的是,样本量尚小,结果也属于探索性免疫原性分析,目前还不能据此认定其临床保护效果优于已上市疫苗。 更受关注的是联合疫苗的II期进展。 2026年9月,三叶草生物宣布,SCB-1022和SCB-1033在澳大利亚开展的II期临床试验取得积极初步结果。根据2026年中报,该研究面向60至85岁老年人,设计招募规模为最多420名;公司已于2026年3月底宣布完成入组。 根据公司公告,接种后第28天,与接种前相比,RSV中和抗体水平约提升6至9倍,hMPV中和抗体水平约提升6至8倍;PIV3中和抗体总体约提升3倍,在基线抗体水平较低的受试者中,提升幅度约为5倍。 公司还披露,在75岁及以上受试者中,未观察到明显的免疫应答减弱;三联疫苗增加PIV3抗原后,也未观察到对RSV和hMPV中和抗体反应的免疫干扰。 从安全性看,两款候选疫苗总体耐受性良好,未报告与疫苗相关的严重不良事件。 生产工艺方面,公司已完成相关抗原组分在2000升生物反应器中的放大生产和多个批次生产。 从初步人体数据到工艺放大,两款联合疫苗都取得了看得见的阶段性进展,已不再停留于产品设想。 这些结果值得肯定,但疫苗走向商业化还需要更多临床验证。 商业化方面同样需要面对强手。GSK、辉瑞和Moderna的RSV疫苗已经进入市场,这些企业在全球临床研究、监管沟通、生产体系,以及医院、接种机构和支付方渠道上都有积累。 对三叶草生物而言,RSV联合疫苗不仅提供了再次展现技术实力的机会,更重要的是,如何将联合疫苗的技术特点转化为切实的产品优势,并进一步建立市场竞争力。 这一挑战,也折射出中国创新疫苗企业普遍面临的发展命题。 即在资金相对充裕、市场预期高涨的阶段,技术平台、研发管线和潜在市场空间足以支撑较高估值;但当市场的关注点转向商业化兑现,企业就必须回答一系列更为现实的问题:技术能否转化为产品,产品能否带来收入,而收入又能否支撑企业的长期发展。 经历行业周期的起伏后,三叶草生物正在逐步化解历史遗留问题,新的研发管线也取得了较为扎实的阶段性进展。 当然,从技术突破走向商业化成功,仍有一段路要走。但相比此前的低谷,三叶草生物已经展现出更多积极变化,也为未来的发展增添了新的想象空间。 频道: 金融财经 本内容由作者授权发布,观点仅代表作者本人,不代表虎嗅立场。 如对本稿件有异议或投诉,请联系 tougao@huxiu.com。 正在改变与想要改变世界的人,都在 虎嗅APP 赞赏 关闭赞赏 开启赞赏 支持一下 修改 确定 评论 登录 后参与评论
